subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should LaunchAgent-managed raw-stream logging fail closed when an operator sets `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=0` or unsets it via `launchctl`, even if a durable service env file, state-dir `.env`, or config env source still contains `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=1`?
rationale: This chooses precedence for a sensitive diagnostic log across launchd inherited env, owner-only service env files, state-dir `.env`, and config env; automation should not silently decide that security boundary.

options.title: Fail Closed On Explicit False
options.body: Treat explicit operator false/unset evidence as disabling raw-stream writes and add Doctor/status/docs proof for cleaning hidden service-env sources.

options.title: Document Durable Source Precedence
options.body: Keep durable service env/config values authoritative, but make Doctor/status identify the active source and document exactly how to remove it.

options.title: Require Live LaunchAgent Repro First
options.body: Hold implementation until a macOS LaunchAgent trace captures process env, generated service env file, and append behavior in one run.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Explicit False
recommendation.body: Treat explicit operator false/unset evidence as disabling raw-stream writes and add Doctor/status/docs proof for cleaning hidden service-env sources.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the best available routing owner from current blame/import history across the raw-stream, LaunchAgent, service-env, and docs files.
